findings: Mean absolute error rises monotonically with frequency: k=1 0.002459, k=2 0.003882, k=4 0.007595, k=8 0.015967.
The k=8 mean absolute error is about 6.49 times the k=1 value, while maximum absolute error rises from 0.01580 to 0.11500.
Error is strongly phase-position dependent rather than uniform. Across all conditions, mean phase-bin error ranges from about 0.00153 to 0.01184.
The phase-bin profile is approximately symmetric, with low error near periodic boundary/zero-crossing regions and larger error in specific interior regions.
These numerical results provide a mechanism consistent with Exp011: adding higher Fourier frequencies can amplify exact-cosine versus Q.ANT evaluation mismatch.
interpretation: The pre-registered hypothesis is supported on the Q.ANT CPU backend. Frequency and periodic argument location both structure the discrepancy. This makes simply increasing Fourier grid size a poor default strategy when training uses exact cosine but evaluation uses calc_kan_layer_fprop.
next_research_direction: Separate bfloat16 argument/parameter quantization from the toolkit periodic-function approximation, then use the measured Q.ANT response to design a training surrogate that is aligned with calc_kan_layer_fprop rather than exact cosine.
limitations: CPU backend only; no photonic hardware performance claim.
Synthetic scalar sweep rather than activation distributions from trained models.
The current experiment combines bfloat16 conversion and the Q.ANT periodic implementation, so it cannot attribute the error to either component separately.
